CaseStudies.Title: Case studies
CaseStudies.Intro: Problem → decision → result. What I did, why I chose it, and the number that came out of it.

Case1.Name: StartCrypto
Case1.Problem: Crypto course with no sales page; conversion depended on referrals and the founder couldn't scale enrollments.
Case1.ProblemMobile: Course with no sales page; couldn't scale enrollments.
Case1.Decision: Conversion-oriented visual copy structure + static Next.js for low LCP. Traded off a CMS (less flexible) in favor of speed and SEO — the right call for a campaign landing page.

Case2.Name: LA Medic Rio
Case2.Problem: Medical equipment company with no digital presence; needed to convey credibility and be found in local search.
Case2.Decision: Semantic institutional site with structured data and on-page SEO, no heavy framework. I prioritized load time and indexing over interactivity — the audience arrives via Google, not an app.

About.Title: About
Paragraphs: I've been a frontend engineer for five years, at the border between engineering and design — where UX decisions become production code.

I like treating performance and conversion as an engineering problem, not luck. I've shipped hundreds of high-converting pages for a US client and built platforms with members areas and dashboards from scratch.
I componentize early, measure what I ship, and treat accessibility as a requirement — not decoration.
